content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] (without display) connected to a [product_name] operator panel. The client reports the program is lost. I see two possibilities: First, they report occasional power outages—the [product_name] is powered by a [company_name] power supply. Could power interruptions cause loss of the program? Second, maybe someone intentionally deleted it using the operator panel menu. The program is password protected, but from the [product_name] manual, it states that after three incorrect password attempts, the program may be deleted. I'm unsure about the operator panel menu—does it have a 'clear program' option? Thanks.

You're correct; it's possible to delete a password-protected program at the [product_name] base module. However, this cannot be done via the connected operator panel. I've encountered similar situations—my investigation showed the operator deleted the program directly on the base module. This issue was addressed by [company_name] with updated versions of both the base module and operator panel. With the newer hardware revision, deletion without the password is not possible. For earlier versions, you could switch the base module to STOP mode from the operator panel but not back to RUN. These settings changed with the update, but both modules must have the correct hardware revision and password protection enabled. Hope this helps.

My [product_name] base module does not have a display, so I don't think the user can delete the program that way. The module and operator panel have the following article numbers: [article_no], [article_no]. How can I check the hardware revision? You mentioned that with any operator panel version, deletion via its menu isn't possible, so program cannot be removed through the missing display or the operator panel. What other causes should I check?

On my base module I see: X I 4 / 5 I 6. I think this indicates hardware revision 3, correct? So, on this version, deletion is possible after 3 failed password attempts, but only if the module has a display, which mine does not. Thanks.

1) The operator panel does not include a 'clear program' function. This can't explain the issue. 2) The program is retained in the [product_name] base module indefinitely; power failures do not affect this. Loss of program only happens by manual intervention. Possible scenarios: 1) Disconnection of the programming cable or interruption during download. 2) Inserting an empty memory card, causing the base module to read and erase its program. 3) Using the 'clear user program and password' feature in the software. 4) Using a copy-protected memory card—removing it would empty the module, but reinserting restores it. To identify hardware revision, check the printed matrix on the device's housing. See [url]. As stated before, hardware revision likely isn't the cause for your issue. Newer revisions brought added features for the operator panel.

The base module wasn't using a memory card, so removing a protected card isn't the cause here. Other possibilities: inserting an empty card or accidental deletion via [product_name] programming software. Consider uploading the program; if prompted for a password, try to clear it via the software. I've asked for the module to be sent back for review. Is there any info I can retrieve from the module besides its current program state? I'm unsure if it's possible to view the last PC connection date.

That's correct. [product_name] does not maintain a history file, so retrieving further details is difficult. You can only see if the module is empty or not; there is no record of the 'last connection.' The programming software, however, shows statistics about the last program modification.
Thank you [user_name] and [user_name] for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are unclear about why the user program in a [product_name] base module without display is lost. There are questions about whether power failure, menu actions, or accidental deletion via software or hardware could be responsible. Various hardware revision levels affect how password protection and program deletion behave, but lack of audit or log features in the modules makes troubleshooting difficult.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] base module to retain its program even during power outages and prevent unauthorized or accidental deletion if password protection is enabled. They also expect to see logs or clear traceability of program changes or deletions.
